judge.evidence_requirement: For every dimension, quote output evidence tied to the supplied immutable target. Doctrine names, unsupported diagrams, and generic recommendations are not evidence.

dimensions.description: The review identifies an immutable existing-code revision, a change-range base/head, or a named design revision with its immutable repository base. It follows affected consumers and paths to evidenced boundaries and keeps proposed versus observed evidence, authority classes, and context limits visible.

Every affected module and the target as a whole receive evidence-backed coverage of supported consumer contracts, effective behavioral coverage, coherent ownership and locality, earned depth, real seams and dependency direction, and proportional change.
Fresh dynamic-behavior, static-structure, Uncle Bob/Clean Architecture, and John Ousterhout/APOSD lenses examine the same immutable target and retain separate evidence-bearing results.

Every source finding keeps its identity and one supported disposition; all credible in-scope findings are reported regardless of severity or pre-existing status, while disagreements and unresolved correction choices remain visible.
The result is a read-only architecture brief: it does not edit code, publish comments without authorization, claim remediation, or substitute for complete ticket Code Review.

evals.name: existing cache architecture review
evals.prompt: Use architecture-review on fictional repository revision 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111. Scope: src/cache and its direct consumers. The cache exposes get, refresh, invalidate, and stats through four pass-through wrappers; callers coordinate stale-entry refresh and each reimplements key normalization. Tests cover cache storage methods but no consumer-visible single-flight or invalidation behavior. Repository authority requires one refresh per key and invalidation after role changes. Review the existing architecture without changing files.
evals.expected_output: A read-only architecture brief traces consumers and duplicated policy, applies all six quality claims, distinguishes shallow wrappers from an earned boundary, runs all four mandatory lenses, and reports every supported in-scope finding.
expectations: The immutable revision and src/cache consumer boundary are explicit.
The review identifies caller-owned refresh coordination and repeated key normalization as leaked knowledge with direct prompt evidence.
Every affected module and the whole target receive all six quality-claim dispositions, including deletion-test and seam-reality evidence.
Dynamic behavior, static structure, Uncle Bob/Clean Architecture, and John Ousterhout/APOSD return separate evidence-bearing results.
Missing consumer-visible single-flight and invalidation proof is treated as an effective behavioral coverage gap rather than inferred from storage-method tests.
Credible in-scope findings remain reported regardless of severity, and the review performs no mutation or remediation.

evals.name: architecture-focused pull-request review
evals.prompt: Use architecture-review on fictional pull-request range 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222..3333333333333333333333333333333333333333. The change adds an EmailSender interface with one production adapter and a test fake, then routes an existing notification policy through three new pass-through services. Requirements preserve notification behavior; repository evidence shows no alternate provider or effect-control problem because the existing mail client is already injected at the policy boundary. Review architecture only and do not publish comments.
evals.expected_output: The review compares base and head, tests whether the new modules earn depth and establish real seams, keeps the fake from proving variation by itself, and returns a read-only brief rather than a full ticket review.
expectations: The exact immutable base/head range and architecture-only intent are preserved.
The review applies the deletion test to all new pass-through services.
A manufactured test fake alone does not establish seam reality or justify the new interface.
The existing injected policy boundary is considered as contrary evidence to the new abstraction.
All four mandatory lenses examine the same range and source findings retain separate identities through reconciliation.
The outcome neither publishes comments nor claims complete ticket Code Review.
